urlScheme:
Base: https://data.binance.vision/data/spot/ is CloudFront in front of S3. Responses carry `Server: AmazonS3`, `X-Cache` and `X-Amz-Cf-Pop`. HEAD works, and so does `Accept-Ranges: bytes`. There is NO `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header, so a browser cannot fetch these files cross-origin.

- Monthly 1m: {base}monthly/klines/{SYM}/1m/{SYM}-1m-{YYYY}-{MM}.zip. Example: https://data.binance.vision/data/spot/monthly/klines/BTCUSDT/1m/BTCUSDT-1m-2024-01.zip
- Checksum companion: the same URL plus `.CHECKSUM`.
  - Size is 88 B for monthly names and 91 B for daily names.
  - It is served as `Content-Type: application/zip` even though it is ASCII text.
- Daily 1m: {base}daily/klines/{SYM}/1m/{SYM}-1m-{YYYY}-{MM}-{DD}.zip, plus `.CHECKSUM`.
  - Use daily files for the current, incomplete month. Today is 2026-10-18: daily files 2026-10-01..2026-10-17 exist, and HEAD on BTCUSDT-1m-2026-10.zip returns 404.
  - Also use them as a fallback for the previous month until its monthly file is published.
- Coverage:
  - BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT monthly 1m runs 2017-08..2026-09 (110 months each). That is 81 months per symbol for 2020-01..2026-09.
  - Daily files start 2017-08-17.
- Publication lag:
  - The README says (README.md:5, https://github.com/binance/binance-public-data/blob/master/README.md): "new `daily` data becoming available the next day and new `monthly` data at the first monday of the month".
  - Observed daily lag (S3 LastModified): every daily file for 2026-09 and 2026-10-01..17 was published 1.4-2.8 h after 00:00 UTC.
  - Observed monthly lag: every monthly file since 2025-06 was published on the first Monday of the next month, 07:12-11:36 UTC. That is 7 h to 6.5 days after month end.
  - Older monthly lags were irregular: 2024-09 took 14.5 days, 2023-01 took 17 days and 2023-08 took 18 days.
  - LastModified records the last re-upload, not the first publication. All monthly files 2020-01..2021-05 show 2021-06-22, and BTCUSDT-1m-2022-03.zip shows 2022-09-02.
- A 404 means "not published yet". The importer should retry it later rather than treat it as an error.
- Schedule the daily run after about 03:00 UTC.
- The S3 listing is at https://s3-ap-northeast-1.amazonaws.com/data.binance.vision?delimiter=/&prefix=data/spot/monthly/klines/BTCUSDT/1m/ (details in the `listing` field).
listing:
The listing is S3 ListObjects v1 XML (ListBucketResult) at https://s3-ap-northeast-1.amazonaws.com/data.binance.vision?delimiter=/&prefix=<prefix>. It is the same endpoint the site's own page uses: BUCKET_URL in https://data.binance.vision/?prefix=... and the createS3QueryUrl/marker logic in https://data.binance.vision/list.js. It also answers `list-type=2` (v2).

Each object has Key, LastModified, ETag, Size and StorageClass. Since 2025-02, objects also carry `<ChecksumAlgorithm>CRC64NVME</ChecksumAlgorithm><ChecksumType>FULL_OBJECT</ChecksumType>`, inserted between ETag and Size.

Pitfalls, each verified:
1. A regex that expects `<ETag>` to be immediately followed by `<Size>` silently drops every object from 2025-02 onward. My first parser stopped at 2025-01 for exactly this reason. Parse each `<Contents>` block field by field.
2. MaxKeys is 1000. The full daily prefix data/spot/daily/klines/BTCUSDT/1m/ returns IsTruncated=true with NextMarker=...BTCUSDT-1m-2018-12-29.zip.CHECKSUM. Paginate with `&marker=<NextMarker>`, or use narrow prefixes such as .../BTCUSDT-1m-2026-10.
3. The bucket name contains dots, so the virtual-hosted URL https://data.binance.vision.s3.ap-northeast-1.amazonaws.com fails TLS (SEC_E_WRONG_PRINCIPAL). Use path-style URLs only.
4. ETag equals the MD5 of the object.
   - Verified on all 3 downloaded files.
   - None of the 162 monthly zips for 2020-01..2026-09 has a multipart ETag.
   - So one listing call per symbol gives size and MD5 for every month, which makes cheap change detection possible.
5. The monthly listing has 220 objects per symbol (110 zips + 110 CHECKSUMs) and is not truncated.

Caveat: issue #511 (https://github.com/binance/binance-public-data/issues/511, open, no answer) asks whether anonymous ListObjects is an approved access method. The importer should therefore not depend on the listing. Build URLs deterministically, treat 404 as "not yet published", and use the listing only as an optional ETag/size manifest.
checksum:
Format: `<64 lowercase hex sha256><two spaces><zip basename>`, with NO trailing newline. This is sha256sum format.

Verified example: BTCUSDT-1m-2026-10-17.zip.CHECKSUM contains "ce5536cff2985e8b1b36c115627c7a30cc8c43d89e2172d5bf5cf3b0dd2fc03a  BTCUSDT-1m-2026-10-17.zip".
- The sha256 of the downloaded zip matches.
- `sha256sum -c` reports OK.

The README documents the same check (README.md:88-97): `sha256sum -c BNBUSDT-1m-2021-01.zip.CHECKSUM`.

Node check, no npm needed:
- Match the text against `/^([0-9a-f]{64}) {2}(\S+)\s*$/`.
- Require group 2 to equal the expected basename.
- Compare group 1 with `crypto.createHash('sha256').update(zipBuf).digest('hex')`.
- Read the body as text even though the Content-Type is application/zip.

Independent cross-check without extra downloads (S3 ETag equals MD5):
- ETHUSDT-1m-2020-06.zip: d5b0e8e41ea4f188b2051467d45012bd
- BTCUSDT-1m-2024-12-31.zip: 8e9ca636c14ba8d8004d190311676b94
- BTCUSDT-1m-2026-10-17.zip (a 2025+ object with CRC64NVME): 34fb47fd8897d117ae72c3e19704ee6d
All three match `md5sum` of the downloaded files.

The CHECKSUM only proves you received what Binance published. The importer still needs:
- the ZIP CRC-32 check (done in the extractor);
- content validation (gaps, duplicates, OHLC).

For a backfill, fetch one CHECKSUM per zip: 196 extra requests of under 100 bytes each.
zipStructure:
The three samples (ETHUSDT 2020-06 monthly, BTCUSDT 2024-12-31 daily, BTCUSDT 2026-10-17 daily) have identical layouts:
- Exactly ONE entry, named `<SYM>-1m-<YYYY-MM[-DD]>.csv`.
- Compression method 8 (deflate).
- General-purpose flags 0x0000:
  - bit 3 is off, so there is NO data descriptor and the CRC and sizes are filled in the local header;
  - not encrypted.
- Version needed 2.0 (0x14); made by Unix 2.0.
- Extra-field length is 0 in both the local and central headers.
- NO ZIP64: the largest CSV is 6,045,956 bytes and there is no ZIP64 EOCD locator.
- No archive comment.

Byte layout:
- Local header at offset 0.
- Data starts at 30+nameLen: 52 for monthly names, 55 for daily names.
- Central directory is 46+nameLen bytes: 68 or 71.
- A 22-byte EOCD sits at end of file.
- Size identity: 65,267 = (30+25) + 65,119 + 71 + 22.

Evidence:
- `unzip -l`
- `unzip -Z -v`, which reports "compression method: deflated", "extended local header: no", "length of extra field: 0 bytes" and "There is no zipfile comment".
- Python `zipfile` run with -I: entries=1, compress_type=8, flag_bits=0x0, extra=0.
- Raw bytes `50 4b 03 04 14 00 00 00 08 00`.

The uncompressed-to-compressed ratio is 3.0-3.4. The DOS modification time is the file-generation time and is irrelevant here.
csvColumns:
There is NO header row: the first line is data in the 2020, 2024 and 2026 samples. A header line is still skipped and reported, defensively. Rows have 12 comma-separated columns, LF line endings and a trailing newline.

README.md:20-25 says the data is "obtained from `/api/v3/klines` API endpoint". Columns:
- 0 `open_time`: epoch, UTC; ms up to 2024, µs from 2025.
- 1-4 `open`, `high`, `low`, `close`: quote currency USDT, last-trade prices, printed with 8 decimals, e.g. "81615.91000000".
- 5 `volume`: base asset.
- 6 `close_time`: open_time + 59,999 ms, or + 59,999,999 µs.
- 7 `quote_asset_volume`
- 8 `number_of_trades`
- 9 `taker_buy_base_asset_volume`
- 10 `taker_buy_quote_asset_volume`
- 11 `ignore`: always "0".

Example 2026 row:
`1792195200000000,81615.91000000,81615.91000000,81602.36000000,81602.36000000,10.01136000,1792195259999999,817033.69934660,557,5.77038000,470920.82646770,0`

The output keeps only columns 0-4, as `[sec, o, h, l, c]`.

Precision: no OHLC value in any sample has more than 2 significant decimals (BTCUSDT 2024 and 2026, ETHUSDT 2020). That gives priceDecimals 2 (tick 0.01) for both symbols. The tested parser counts any value that exceeds the configured precision.

Semantics: these are trade-price candles, not bid/ask. Dukascopy forex/gold data is BID, so the trade engine needs an explicit spread rule for crypto. Crypto trades 24/7, so the expected grid is every UTC minute.
timestampUnits:
CONFIRMED with the files and the official notice.

From the files:
- BTCUSDT-1m-2024-12-31: all 1,440 rows have 13-digit ms open_time (1735603200000), and close-open = 59,999.
- BTCUSDT-1m-2026-10-17: all 1,440 rows have 16-digit µs open_time (1792195200000000), and close-open = 59,999,999.
- ETHUSDT-1m-2020-06: 13-digit ms.

Official notice:
- README.md:11: "**Note**: The timestamp for SPOT Data from January 1st 2025 onwards will be in microseconds." (https://github.com/binance/binance-public-data/blob/master/README.md)
- It was added on 2025-01-09 in commit de6bdec, "Microsecond update" (https://github.com/binance/binance-public-data/commit/de6bdec7520bcae888d66c362257f120dfc9d65b). The same commit changed the README kline example to 1735689600000000.
- That followed issue #386 (https://github.com/binance/binance-public-data/issues/386), where a maintainer replied "it has been updated".

The REST API stays in ms by default; µs is opt-in per the spot API CHANGELOG entry of 2024-12-17 (https://github.com/binance/binance-spot-api-docs/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md). So the archive files and the API differ.

Do not reuse the current conversion `time: Math.floor(k[0] / 1000)` (src/pages/backtest.astro:371) on archive data. Applied to µs values, it would produce dates tens of thousands of years in the future.

Normalize per row:
- 13 digits: divide by 1e3. 16 digits: divide by 1e6. Any other length: reject.
- Equivalently, take the first 10 digits as epoch seconds (valid for 2001-2286) and require the remaining digits to be zeros and seconds % 60 == 0.

Store Unix seconds UTC. That is what lightweight-charts and the current page use, and what the month and day boundaries in Date.UTC are based on.

I did not sample a 2025-01+ monthly file because of the file cap, so detect the unit per row. A mixed-unit test passes.

Issue #474 (https://github.com/binance/binance-public-data/issues/474) shows the failure mode: a user's unit mistake made 2025+ data look like a 2,750x volume drop.
quality:
Verified in the samples:
- 0 duplicates, 0 out-of-order rows, 0 misaligned timestamps.
- OHLC is always consistent (low <= open/close <= high, all > 0).
- 0 zero-volume rows; 1 flat candle in ETH 2020-06.
- No price exceeds 2 decimals.
- Both daily files have the full 1,440 of 1,440 minutes.

VERIFIED GAP: ETHUSDT-1m-2020-06 has 42,990 of 43,200 rows. Its only gap is 2020-06-28 02:00-05:29 UTC (210 min). That matches Binance's announced spot upgrade: start 02:00 UTC, trading resumed 05:30 UTC (https://www.binance.com/en/support/announcement/binance-spot-trading-system-upgrade-complete-2020-06-28-7d9d22ad6232459984c5ea30ea0986af). Halted periods simply have no rows, with no filler candles, and they hit every symbol at once.

Candidate exchange-wide halts 2020-2023 (taken from announcement/news summaries, NOT verified in files):

- 2020-12-25: about 02:00-03:00 UTC (https://www.binance.com/en/support/announcement/binance-spot-trading-system-upgrade-complete-2020-12-25-38b072b7f1004812a16f9bbd53206ca7).
- 2021-03-06: from 02:00 UTC, about 1 h plus 30 min cancel-only (https://www.binance.com/en/support/announcement/binance-spot-trading-system-upgrade-notice-2021-03-06-f02cab4e685b46da803bb0a680546d4b).
- 2021-04-20: 02:00-04:30 UTC (https://www.binance.com/en/support/announcement/binance-spot-trading-system-upgrade-complete-2021-04-20-1ff4855808344ad49265ea14a03b32bb).
- 2021-04-25: upgrade notice (https://www.binance.com/en/support/announcement/binance-spot-trading-system-upgrade-notice-2021-04-25-849160fe70214641baa6385619595aa1).
- 2021-08-13: 02:00-06:30 UTC (https://www.binance.com/en/support/announcement/3ef1861772a44c67acc2c9f5ec9f87e4).
- 2021-09-29: 07:00-09:00 UTC (https://www.binance.com/en-TR/support/announcement/binance-spot-trading-system-upgrade-complete-2021-09-29-f72eB94584fA47A586127fF5149eF83c).
- 2023-03-24: about 12:20-14:00 UTC, matching-engine bug. Issue #501 says the BTCUSDT 1h 13:00 candle is missing from both the API and the archive (https://github.com/binance/binance-public-data/issues/501). The 2023-03-24 daily zip is 65,200 B against 70-73 KB for neighbouring days.

Reported archive-only gap: #400 says BTCUSDT 1h/1m data for 2024-10-28 is missing from the archive while the API has it (https://github.com/binance/binance-public-data/issues/400). This is unverified; that day's zip size looks normal. Older reports are out of range: 2017-09-06 (#374), 2018-02-08 (#379), 2018-06-26 (#434).

Duplicates: none found here, but a spot 1d duplicate was reported in 2022 (#191), so dedupe anyway.

Archive files can change. README.md:99-106 says "Archived files may be updated at a later date as a result of recently discovered issues" (the 2022-08-08 kline update was "Fixed inconsistent data"), and BTCUSDT-1m-2022-03.zip was re-uploaded on 2022-09-02. So store each month's source sha256 and ETag in a manifest, and optionally re-check ETags.

Detection (implemented in parse-validate.mjs and tested):
- Build the expected 24/7 UTC minute grid for each month, from month start to min(month end, coverage end), and report gaps as [from, to, minutes].
- Count, and keep the first of, duplicates. Count conflicts separately when the duplicate values differ.
- Count out-of-order rows and re-sort.
- Count and drop:
  - misaligned timestamps;
  - rows outside the month;
  - rows with invalid OHLC;
  - malformed rows (wrong digit count or non-numeric fields).
- Count precision overflow.
- Never synthesize missing candles.
- Optionally tag gaps that match a known-outage table, so the report separates "exchange halted" from "unexplained".
- The browser aggregator must tolerate gaps: bucket by floor(t/tf)*tf.

Ongoing traffic: about 4 GETs a day (2 symbols, each a roughly 70 KB daily zip plus its CHECKSUM), plus 4 GETs a month (about 4 MB) to replace the dailies with the monthly file.

CSV parsed: 3.0-3.4x the zip size, so about 1.0-1.17 GB in total, handled one month at a time with at most about 6.3 MB in memory.

Candles: 2,482 days (2020-01-01..2026-10-17) x 1,440 = 3,574,080 per symbol, 7,148,160 in total, minus outage gaps.

Output size, compact JSON [[sec,o,h,l,c]] with gzip -9, measured:
- 9.07 B/candle for the full ETHUSDT 2020-06 month (1,734,408 B JSON to 389,743 B gz).
- 14.36 B/candle for BTCUSDT 2024-12-31 (20,678 B per day).
- 10.79 B/candle for BTCUSDT 2026-10-17 (15,543 B).

Projected Storage:
- About 0.39-0.64 MB per symbol-month.
- 164 objects (82 months x 2), about 65-103 MB in total. That is roughly 0.20-0.29x the source zips, which is consistent.
- Uncompressed JSON is about 1.7-2.1 MB per month (40-48 B/candle).

Per replay session: one month is about 0.4-0.65 MB of transfer, plus one prefetched neighbouring month.

Governing document: "BINANCE VISION DATASET TERMS", Version 1.0, Last Updated August 26, 2026. The site header links "Terms of Use" to https://data.binance.vision/terms-of-use.html, which embeds https://data.binance.vision/Binance_Vision-Terms_of_Use.pdf. The PDF text is identical to https://github.com/binance/binance-public-data/blob/master/TERMS_AND_CONDITIONS.md, which was added on 2026-09-30 (commit bd110bb). README.md:108-110 points to it. The README's "Licence: MIT" (README.md:116-117) covers the repository, not the data.

Key quotes from TERMS_AND_CONDITIONS.md:
- §3.1 (line 31): "Datasets are provided to you under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International Public License ("CC BY-NC-SA 4.0")".
- §3.2 (line 33): "You agree to be fully bound by the terms of CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and these Vision Dataset Terms upon downloading, caching, querying, or otherwise utilizing the Datasets."
- §3.4 (line 37): "Commercial licensing is strictly excluded under this agreement; any commercial utilization requires a separate, written enterprise data license agreement executed with Binance."
- §4.1 (line 41): "Permitted non-commercial uses are limited to academic research, non-monetized open educational projects, algorithmic historical backtesting for purely personal non-production research, and non-commercial open-source data science evaluations."
- §4.3 (line 45): "You shall not license, sub-license, sell, rent, lease, host, or commercially exploit the Datasets or any derivative real-time or historical data feeds."
- §4.4 (line 47): "You shall not integrate the Datasets into commercial financial products, hedge fund management tools, paid subscription newsletters, or commercial trading bot platforms."
- §4.5 (line 49): redistributed derivative works must credit "Binance Vision" and stay under the identical CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence.
- §2.4 (line 27): derived data, "including charts", is governed by these Terms.
- §7.1-7.3 (lines 71-75): obey posted rate limits; no scraping meant to get around them; Binance may ban IPs.
- §8.3 (line 83): do not use the name "Binance" to market commercial applications.
- §1.4 (line 15): amendments apply prospectively, so data downloaded now falls under v1.0.

Why this applies here:
- Wawe Journal is monetized. The premium plan is sold through NOWPayments (PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md:39, :211, :267, :302).
- Storing Binance-derived candles in Supabase Storage and serving them to logged-in users means hosting a derivative historical feed inside a commercial product (§3.4, §4.3, §4.4). That holds even if /backtest itself is free.
- It is not "purely personal non-production research" (§4.1).

Precedent:
- Issue #478 is nearly the same case: "TradeTrace, a subscription-based trading journal, historical chart replay, backtesting..." It downloads and checksum-verifies Vision klines, stores them in private cloud storage and shows them to authenticated paying users. A Binance contributor replied only "please refer to the TERMS_AND_CONDITIONS.md document" and closed the issue on 2026-10-13 (https://github.com/binance/binance-public-data/issues/478).
- Issue #482 (paid replay software where users download the files themselves) got the same reply (https://github.com/binance/binance-public-data/issues/482).
- Issue #514 points out there is no published contact for the enterprise licence (https://github.com/binance/binance-public-data/issues/514).

Fetching directly in the browser does not avoid this. There are no CORS headers, and §4.4 would still apply.

Options for the owner:
- (a) Get a written enterprise data licence from Binance first.
- (b) Use a commercially licensed crypto 1m data source.
- (c) Launch forex/gold first and add crypto later. Another track is checking the Dukascopy terms.

If a licence is obtained, also add the attribution and licence notice the terms require.

report:
Binance track: findings.

1) LEGAL BLOCKER, the owner must decide first.
- Since 2026-08-26, data.binance.vision is under the "Binance Vision Dataset Terms" v1.0: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (https://data.binance.vision/Binance_Vision-Terms_of_Use.pdf, https://github.com/binance/binance-public-data/blob/master/TERMS_AND_CONDITIONS.md).
- They forbid hosting, commercial exploitation and integration into commercial financial products (§4.3, §4.4). Commercial use needs a separate written enterprise licence (§3.4).
- Wawe Journal sells a premium plan (PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md:39, :302). Storing Binance-derived candles in Supabase Storage for logged-in users therefore conflicts with the terms.
- A near-identical subscription trading-journal replay product (issue #478) got only a pointer to the terms, and the issue was closed.
- Options: (a) get a written enterprise licence before importing; (b) use a licensed crypto data vendor; (c) launch forex/gold first.
- Everything below is technically ready, assuming this is resolved.

2) Source mechanics (verified).
- Deterministic URLs: https://data.binance.vision/data/spot/monthly/klines/{SYM}/1m/{SYM}-1m-YYYY-MM.zip, the same for daily as .../daily/.../{SYM}-1m-YYYY-MM-DD.zip, each with a `.CHECKSUM` (sha256sum format, no trailing newline).
- Monthly files exist through 2026-09. The current month comes from daily files (2026-10-01..17 exist).
- Daily files land about 1.5-3 h after UTC midnight. Monthly files land on the first Monday, 07-12 UTC (consistent since 2025-06; earlier up to 18 days late). So fall back to daily files for the previous month until the monthly file appears.
- The S3 listing is optional and has three traps: CRC64NVME elements since 2025-02 break naive regexes; it pages at 1000 keys; only path-style URLs work.
- ETag equals MD5, which is handy for change detection. Files can be republished (README.md:99-106).

3) ZIP.
- One deflate-compressed CSV entry, no data descriptor, no extra field, no ZIP64, no comment.
- A 58-line Node extractor using zlib.inflateRawSync and zlib.crc32 (Node >= 22.2) produces output byte-identical to `unzip -p`.

4) CSV.
- No header and 12 columns; only columns 0-4 are kept.
- Timestamps CONFIRMED: ms through 2024-12-31 and µs from 2025-01-01 (README.md:11, commit de6bdec of 2025-01-09, issue #386).
- Normalize per row by digit count, 13 or 16; reject anything else. Store Unix seconds UTC.
- Do not reuse `Math.floor(k[0] / 1000)` from src/pages/backtest.astro:371.
- Prices have at most 2 decimals (tick 0.01) for both symbols.
- Values are last-trade prices, not bid, so the crypto spread rule must be defined separately from Dukascopy's bid-based rule.

Recommended Binance part of the import script (Node, no npm):
- Run per symbol and per UTC month M from 2020-01 to the current month.
- Skip M if candles/{SYM}/{M}.json.gz exists and its manifest is not marked partial.
- For a past M:
  - GET the CHECKSUM and the monthly zip; a 404 means fall back to that month's daily files.
  - Verify sha256, extract, then parseKlinesCsv.
  - Gzip [[sec,o,h,l,c]] and upsert the object.
  - Record source (monthly/daily), sha256, ETag, rows, missing minutes and gaps in the manifest.
- The current month is rebuilt from daily files up to the last published day and marked partial.
- Download sequentially or with concurrency of 2 or less, with retry/backoff; 404 means "later" (terms §7).
- Each month is processed and uploaded independently, so a crashed run simply resumes at the first missing or partial month.
